purpose: Define navigation links/routes separately from state-changing actions so route changes never implicitly execute commands and action controls never masquerade as ordinary navigation.

topics.name: Navigation and Action Separation
topics.purpose: Define navigation links/routes separately from state-changing actions so route changes never implicitly execute commands and action controls never masquerade as ordinary navigation.

semantics.navigation_rule: Navigation changes human-facing location/view using exact nanoCMS route/resource bindings.
semantics.action_rule: State-changing actions invoke explicit canonical operations.
semantics.link_rule: Ordinary links are non-mutating by default.
semantics.method_rule: Mutation semantics are never hidden in an apparently read-only route/navigation transition.
semantics.route_rule: Route identity and represented resource identity remain distinct.
semantics.history_rule: Browser history/back/forward does not repeat state-changing operations merely by navigation replay.
semantics.confirmation_rule: Any confirmation requirement belongs to the operation/profile, not to visual link styling.
semantics.authority_rule: Route accessibility and operation authorization remain separately evaluated.

invariants.rule: Expose Elements are reusable human-interface primitives that project or invoke explicitly bound semantics; visual form, nesting, focus, color, position or enabled-looking state never creates ownership, authority or domain meaning.

prose.summary: Define navigation links/routes separately from state-changing actions so route changes never implicitly execute commands and action controls never masquerade as ordinary navigation.
